body.name: Branch-dual saddle handle for unrestricted multi-survivor two-batch designs
body.construction: For each \(m\in\{2,\ldots,K-1\}\), parameterize an unrestricted two-batch top-\(m\) design by \(0<\rho<1\), an interior first-batch allocation \(a\in\mathcal W\), and a branch-specific allocation \(b_J\in\operatorname{int}\Sigma_J\) for every \(J\in\mathcal J_m\).  Thus \(D=D(\rho,a,\{b_J\}_{J\in\mathcal J_m})\in\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all,multi}}\).  For a fixed tuple, replace \(q_i(\rho)\) by \(\rho a_i\), \(r_i(J;\rho)\) by \((1-\rho)b_{J,i}\), and \(n_i(J;\rho)\) by \(\rho a_i+(1-\rho)b_{J,i}\) in the survivor-set programs of \(\text{def:branch-programs}\), whose Gaussian objectives depend on the known variance vector \(s\).  This produces, for each best-exclusion or terminal branch, an explicit convex quadratic objective subject to linear inequalities.  The full-class handle jointly optimizes the resulting finite branch minimum over the discrete choice of \(m\), over \(\rho\), \(a\), and \(\{b_J\}\), and against all \(\mu\) having a unique best arm.  Its proposed optimality certificate consists of primal branch witnesses and feasible Lagrange multipliers for the branch polyhedra that give matching bounds on the robust ratio to \(I_w(\mu)\).  Neither a minimax interchange nor the value \(G_{\mathrm{multi}}\) is imposed by this definition.
